checkpoint_controls_reviewed: Per-run flock blocks duplicate optimizers for a run.
Checkpoint restore validates metadata, config hash, normalizer provenance, initial weights, and sample count; restores optimizer, EMA, and random streams.
Latest/milestone checkpoints use atomic saves; uncommitted log tails are archived before resume.
Completed training/evaluation artifacts are identity/hash checked before reuse.
Training readiness requires complete frozen data, initial proposal freeze, and successful implementation audit.

focused_tests.command: pixi run --no-install --frozen python -m pytest -q tests/round3/test_process_cleanup.py tests/round3/test_integration.py -k "process or interrupt or child or owned_group or partial_data or stale_recovery or authorized_devices or individual_worker or candidate_requires" --disable-warnings -p no:cacheprovider

checks.prior_cross_process_resume_evidence: round3/audits/cross_process_resume.json: 100+100 debug updates matched an independent 200-update reference for model, EMA, loader RNG, diffusion RNG, and pairing; not repeated in this review.

findings.before: A mocked interrupt in _child confirmed SIGINT was sent but the exception escaped while its worker remained alive, permitting the parent GPU lease to unwind before checkpoint saving finished.
findings.repair: The CLI now waits for the launcher and all live members of its owned process group before propagating the original exception or clearing its launcher claim. Repeated interrupts, a group-exit signal race, and zombie group members are handled.
findings.validation: Four synthetic cases plus five existing scheduler safety checks passed. No real process signal, optimizer update, or simulator episode was used.

findings.change_scope: No SIGKILL recovery refactor was authorized for this bounded fix. Existing live schedulers retain their loaded earlier CLI and were not interrupted.
findings.detail: Workers launched under ROUND3_GPU_LEASE_PID rely on the scheduler-held GPU lock. Abrupt scheduler death can release that lock while its worker survives; stale-run reconciliation preserves a live run, but does not reserve its GPU against a different pending run.
findings.recovery_requirement: After abrupt parent termination, inspect recorded worker/launcher PIDs and actual GPU processes before launching replacement queues; wait for owned surviving workers to exit. Preserve unrelated processes. A future durable worker-owned/inherited lease can close this gap.

findings.detail: Four migrated protocol manifests retain old source_file/XML paths as provenance. Runtime readers use observation schema and other metadata and do not open those old paths. Round1 progress output retains an old display-only project path, while ROOT is derived from the relocated source file. Historical handoff and recovery documents retain prior roots/GPU limits.
findings.recommendation: Keep immutable provenance and historical sources unchanged. Root README/AGENTS/LIVE_EXECUTION give current root and GPU0–5 commands. The Pixi workspace name agent_training is a package/workspace label, not a directory dependency.

findings.detail: The migration audit records that historical runs/checkpoints were absent in the received repository. Existing historical reports are preserved; this review does not claim their missing checkpoints are recoverable from disk.

scope: Root relocation, Git recoverability, runtime entry points, and orderly checkpoint/GPU cleanup; no training, evaluation, installation, or sealed test contents accessed.
